newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem denies alleged bribery meeting.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem denies alleged bribery meeting.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem denied having participated in a meeting in which former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo alleges they discussed the payment of bribes in a scandal involving a state-owned bank and the U.S. computer giant IBM's local branch.
"I never was at such a meeting," Menem told the daily Clarin in an interview. "We never talked about that."
Clarin also printed Cavallo's testimony on Monday to a federal judge in which the former superminister alleged that Menem's chief of staff Alberto Kohan was aware of the payment of bribes.

According to the printed testimony, Cavallo said that last year he, Menem and Kohan met and he walked out convinced that Kohan knew that government officials had paid bribes to secure the deal between Banco Nacion and IBM.
Kohan denied such a meeting on Tuesday, when the first elements of the testimony to judge Adolfo Bagnasco were leaked to the press. He also indicated that he may sue Cavallo.
Cavallo is abroad and his spokesman has declined to comment on the case.
A federal court last month confirmed the indictment of 11 of the 30 former IBM Argentina and former Banco Nacion employees who Bagnasco had indicted in the case.

Banco Nacion last June cancelled the deal and demanded that IBM refund $82 million in payments, but the firm fired back, suing the bank in July for more than $86 million alleging "wrongful revocation" of the contract.
Then in August, Banco Nacion countersued the firm for $174 million. IBM denies any malicious intent, although it has admitted to errors.
Other IBM Argentina deals are under separate court investigations.

Cavallo, who was fired in July by Menem, launched a drive against alleged corruption in the government earlier this month , accusing two ministers of manipulating judges and trying to cover up graft investigations.
